releaseNotes:
- Makes AgentOS the single approval authority for both Codex and OpenCode: policy-approved tools continue without user interruption, while reviewable operations create one AgentOS approval and resume the same native tool call after the user decides
- Keeps the prepared Harness session, sandbox process, bridge, and model lease attached while a Run waits for approval, preventing duplicated assistant turns, repeated processing indicators, interrupted commands, and approval continuations that silently start a second execution
- Adapts OpenCode permission events into the same ordered tool-call and approval stream used by Codex, including forwarding external-directory decisions to AgentOS instead of letting the native Harness apply a separate hidden policy
- Treats shell no-op commands and output redirection to `/dev/null`, standard streams, or existing file descriptors as non-mutating, so read-only system inspection does not request high-risk approval merely because it suppresses diagnostic output
- Resumes browser and External SDK event streams without emitting a second execution or assistant start, and patches the persisted assistant message during approval continuation instead of rendering a duplicate response
- Enables Linux systemd user lingering during bootstrap installation so the AgentOS service survives the final SSH logout and starts with the host; online, local-archive, and offline bootstrap sources share this behavior
- Ships with AgentOS Runtime `1.0.0-beta.8`, whose OpenCode Bootstrap contains the matching approval-authority and permission-ordering Bridge recipe
- Does not change the public TypeScript or Java SDK request/response schemas

### Verification

- Passed TypeScript checking, the complete production build, and all 336 TypeScript, Server, UI, and TypeScript SDK tests, including approval-policy, Run executor, OpenCode adapter, Cube lifecycle, External SDK, installer, and online/offline upgrade coverage
- Passed the Sandbox VMM Go suite and all 10 Java 8 SDK tests
- Passed the 67-check release source preflight and installer shell validation
- Verified all four real browser paths against a prepared Cube template: Codex and OpenCode read-only commands ran without approval, while each high-risk command showed one approval and continued in the same assistant response; the browser console remained free of errors
